strengths: Clear empirical observation that reasoning uncertainty is localized to high-entropy tokens, well-demonstrated in Figure 1
Practical training-free method that adds minimal inference overhead (only 4-25% of tokens require CFG)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse benchmarks (general, coding, math/science), multiple model scales (8B-32B), and both base/reasoning variants
Thorough ablation studies and analysis including entropy threshold effects, CFG strength tuning, prompt variants, and principled justification for entropy-based selection (Figure 5)
Well-written paper with effective visualizations and clear presentation of the core concepts
weaknesses: Limited novelty: combines established techniques (entropy-based selection from Li et al. 2025/Wang et al. 2025, CFG from Ho & Salimans 2022, LLM-CFG from Sanchez et al. 2023); main contribution is incremental combination

Concerning vanilla CFG baseline: frequently underperforms direct inference (e.g., Qwen3-8B-Base MMLU-Pro: 50.28 vs 56.81, Qwen3-14B-Reasoning WinoGrande: 66.22 vs 75.14), raising questions about implementation correctness and whether improvements stem from selective intervention or VC failures

Modest empirical improvements: averages of 0.39-1.8% across model variants; only specialized benchmarks show larger gains (e.g., GPQA-Diamond +6.57); most results are single-run without error bars or statistical significance testing

Hyperparameter sensitivity undermines practical applicability: entropy threshold τ varies per model type (1.5 for base vs 1.0 for reasoning) with non-monotonic behavior; CFG strength ω requires tuning; no principled guidance for selecting hyperparameters on new models

Lack of theoretical justification: 'OUTPUT ERROR' design appears ad-hoc (why these words?); explanation that it 'constructs more informative unconditional space' is vague; limited systematic exploration of prompt variants (only 4 in Figure 3c)

Technical clarity gaps: KV-cache reuse mechanism poorly explained (are separate forward passes needed? how does this differ computationally from vanilla CFG?); Equation 1 uses log probabilities while typical LLM-CFG manipulates logits directly; uncertainty threshold application strategy unclear
Limited analysis of failure modes: no discussion of when MTI underperforms or hurts accuracy; no per-domain analysis of which tasks benefit most/least
Incomplete stochastic sampling evaluation: main results use greedy decoding; stochastic sampling results only for AIME2024 despite modern systems using sampling
Missing comparisons with other selective guidance methods, entropy-aware approaches, or recent test-time reasoning strategies

strengths: Clear empirical motivation from Figure 1 showing high-entropy tokens drive reasoning failures
Comprehensive experimental coverage across multiple domains (general, coding, math), model sizes (8B-32B), and variants (base vs. reasoning)
Practical efficiency: achieves improvements by intervening on only 1-4% of tokens, training-free and easily integrable
Useful qualitative analysis including entropy distributions (Figure 5), word clouds (Figure 4), and case studies (Figure 6)
Reasonable ablation studies on entropy threshold, CFG strength, and negative prompt choice
Consistent improvements across diverse benchmarks demonstrate generalization within the tested domain
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution (selective CFG application) is a straightforward optimization of vanilla CFG; entropy-based token selection has been explored in prior work

Weak theoretical justification: unclear whether high entropy is a cause or symptom of errors; the claim that 'OUTPUT ERROR' approximates unconditional space lacks rigorous grounding; mechanism of KV cache reuse with modified input is underspecified

Weak experimental baselines: Vanilla CFG (VC) applying uniformly to all tokens is known to be inefficient; no comparison with other test-time methods (speculative decoding, draft-and-verify, alternative entropy-based approaches, or sampling baselines)

Modest and potentially non-significant improvements: most gains are 1-2%; only AIME2024 uses multiple seeds; no standard deviations or significance tests reported; many benchmark improvements are marginal or inconsistent across models
Hyperparameter sensitivity: different optimal τ values across models (1.5 vs. 1.0) and ω sensitivity (1.2 vs. 1.8) suggest per-model tuning is required, limiting generalizability
Selection bias in methodology: high entropy → apply CFG → token changes → answer improves is somewhat circular; no evidence that selective intervention is better than random or alternative strategies

Limited exploration of design choices: 'OUTPUT ERROR' tested only against 'OUTPUT TRUE'; other negative prompts and unconditional approximations unexplored; no analysis of what tokens the model actually generates with this prompt

Reproducibility concerns: implementation details underspecified (how exactly is 'OUTPUT ERROR' injected?), code availability not mentioned, greedy vs. sampling inconsistency between main results and AIME2024 experiments, configuration details sparse
Narrow evaluation scope: only Qwen3 models tested; generalization to other model families (LLaMA, Mistral, etc.) is unclear; single case study (Figure 6) insufficient for understanding failure modes

Statistical rigor: most benchmarks use single runs without variance reporting; improvements lack significance testing; Figure 1 analysis uses total answer entropy, making causality for individual tokens unclear

strengths: Clear and well-motivated empirical observation: localized reasoning uncertainty in high-entropy tokens is compelling and well-demonstrated in Figure 1
Practical and efficient design: selective CFG application achieves +1.35% improvement while using only 4.2% of tokens, with clever KV-cache reuse avoiding dual-cache overhead
Comprehensive experimental validation across 8 benchmarks, 3 model sizes, and both base/reasoning variants with thorough ablation studies on entropy threshold, CFG strength, and negative prompts
Strong consistent improvements across diverse task categories (general, math/science, coding) suggesting robustness beyond specific domains
Well-executed empirical analysis including principled justification via entropy-effect distribution (Figure 5), word-cloud visualization of vocabulary changes, and concrete case studies
Training-free and reproducible: no fine-tuning required with detailed experimental setup and configuration files provided
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: combines existing techniques (entropy-based selection, CFG, KV-cache reuse) without fundamental innovation; entropy-based token selection and CFG are both from prior work
Narrow evaluation scope: limited to Qwen3 model family; generalization to other architectures (GPT-4, Llama3, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek-R1) is unknown and critical for impact claims
Insufficient theoretical foundation: causal claim that high-entropy tokens cause errors lacks rigorous justification; why 'OUTPUT ERROR' effectively approximates unconditional space is unexplained
No comparison with related test-time methods: Self-consistency, Reflexion, and Tree of Thoughts are mentioned but not empirically compared; 'orthogonal' claim needs validation

Incomplete inference cost analysis: claims of 'negligible overhead' lack quantitative support; no wall-clock timing measurements or detailed cost breakdowns provided despite additional entropy computation and forward passes
Hyperparameter sensitivity: optimal τ and ω vary significantly across models (τ: 1.5 vs 1.0; ω: 1.2 vs 1.8), requiring validation data and undermining 'plug-and-play' applicability claims
Missing key ablations: no random CFG control to isolate entropy-based selection gains; insufficient exploration of alternative negative prompts beyond 'OUTPUT ERROR' vs 'OUTPUT TRUE'
Statistical rigor lacking: most improvements lack confidence intervals or significance testing; only AIME2024 uses multiple runs; unclear whether 1-5% improvements are statistically significant
Modest improvements in absolute terms (1.35% average, 5% on AIME2024) with limited analysis of practical significance relative to inference cost
Limited negative prompt design guidance: unclear how to construct effective prompts for domains beyond mathematical reasoning; generalization principles absent

strengths: Clear and well-motivated core insight: High-entropy tokens concentrate errors in LLM reasoning, with compelling empirical evidence in Figure 1. This observation is intuitive and strongly supported.
Practical efficiency design: KV-cache reuse via negative-prompt injection cleverly avoids dual-cache overhead of standard CFG while remaining compatible with modern inference frameworks (vLLM).

Comprehensive empirical validation: Experiments span multiple model families (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, Ling-mini), diverse benchmarks across general/coding/STEM categories, and even extension to VLMs. Comparison with SOTA methods (Table 5) shows competitive performance.

Thorough ablation studies: Systematic analysis of entropy threshold τ, CFG hyperparameter ω, negative prompt semantics, and correlation between token entropy and CFG effectiveness (Figure 4). Clear unimodal patterns enable principled threshold selection.

Insightful supplementary analysis: Word-cloud visualization (Figure 5) reveals lexical diversity improvements; case studies (Figure 6) illustrate concrete advantages over vanilla CFG (e.g., avoiding repetitive loops). Analysis of entropy scopes (Table 6) clarifies why selective intervention matters.

Reproducibility and clarity: Implementation details provided, OpenCompass configuration files specified, code availability mentioned. Generally clear writing with good motivation and effective visualizations.
weaknesses: Weak theoretical justification for negative-prompt mechanism: The paper assumes that prepending 'OUTPUT ERROR' to conditional KV cache effectively approximates unconditional distributions but provides no formal analysis or empirical validation of approximation quality. What distribution is actually being computed? How close is it to true unconditional?

Overstated efficiency claims: Table 3 shows MTI latency is often not better than DI (6081s for Qwen-14B vs. 4547s for DI). Claims of 'minimal overhead' and 'negligible computational overhead' are contradicted by mixed results. Shorter outputs confound method efficiency with task difficulty.

Hyperparameter tuning requirement contradicts parameter-free claims: Despite claiming robustness without 'meticulous tuning,' entropy threshold τ still requires cross-validation with clear unimodal patterns. Section 6 acknowledges needing 'a small subset of data to sweep for τ'—this is parameter tuning. No principled method provided for threshold selection without validation data.

Insufficient analysis of vanilla CFG underperformance: VC severely underperforms in many cases (e.g., 29.29%→32.32% on GPQA-Diamond). Why does standard CFG fail so dramatically? Possible implementation issues? This undermines the fairness of comparisons and raises questions about the baseline.

Negative prompt semantics still somewhat arbitrary: While 'OUTPUT ERROR' generalizes, Table 8 shows task-specific prompts are notably better (94.20% vs. 93.60% for math). The paper doesn't explain mechanistically why negative prompting works or explore design space thoroughly. Is this exploiting model artifacts?

Limited theoretical novelty: Core components (CFG, entropy-based selection) exist individually. Main contribution is selective application + KV-reuse, which is practical but conceptually incremental. Limited new insights into LLM reasoning mechanisms.

Statistical rigor concerns: No confidence intervals, significance tests, or standard deviations reported. Some improvements are modest (+1.99% on VaBenchPoint). AIME2024 results show mean over 8 runs but no variance analysis. Unclear if improvements are statistically significant.

Scope limitations of main experiments: Table 1 uses only greedy search (reducing generalizability). Stochastic decoding only evaluated on AIME2024. Unclear interaction with other decoding strategies (beam search, nucleus sampling). Method tested only on recent models.

Superficial failure case analysis: Limitations section (Section 6) is brief and doesn't deeply explore when selective CFG might fail. No pathological case analysis. Figure 6 case study is illustrative but anecdotal. No discussion of when high-entropy tokens should NOT be modified.

Vanilla CFG comparison fairness unclear: Table 6 shows VC at 73.34% vs. DI at 73.75% on AIME2024 (essentially tied). If vanilla CFG barely underperforms DI, is the distinction between VC and MTI truly fundamental or just better tuning? Raises questions about comparison validity.

strengths: Clear empirical observation: Figure 1 effectively motivates the approach by showing high-entropy tokens correlate with reasoning errors
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple models (Qwen3, DeepSeek, Ling), diverse benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA, MATH, coding, AIME), thorough ablations on τ, ω, and negative prompts
Practical engineering solution: KV cache reuse strategy is well-motivated and addresses real deployment constraints without dual-branch overhead
Consistent empirical improvements: Gains hold across general, coding, and STEM tasks with multiple model scales and datasets
Detailed analysis: Includes word clouds, entropy distributions (Fig. 4), case studies, and extension to vision-language models
Reproducibility: OpenCompass configuration files, eight independent runs on AIME2024, reported testing details
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Combines three existing techniques (entropy-based selection, CFG, negative prompting) without deep conceptual innovation; the KV cache optimization is engineering, not science

Weak theoretical foundation: No principled explanation for why 'OUTPUT ERROR' works as a negative prompt; lacks grounding unlike diffusion model CFG which trains on null conditions; Appendix A.6 shows task-specific prompts work better, contradicting universality

Causality confusion: Figure 1 shows correlation (high entropy ↔ errors) but paper treats as causation; no intervention study proving that fixing high-entropy tokens independently improves outcomes; analysis limited to AIME2024

Hyperparameter tuning contradicts 'training-free' claim: Despite acknowledgment in Section 6, method introduces entropy threshold τ requiring tuning; Figure 3a shows clear sensitivity; no principled method for τ selection provided; practitioners must sweep manually

Methodological issues: (1) Main results use greedy search; generalization to sampling unclear; (2) Vanilla CFG baseline is weak strawman—applies guidance uniformly which the paper proves suboptimal; (3) No statistical significance testing despite variance in results (e.g., DS-R1-7B AIME2024: 54-63% range)

Misleading efficiency claims: 'Minimal' CFG usage is 21.8-31.2% of tokens (Table 1); vanilla CFG baseline shows suspicious latency (12411s), suggesting unfair comparison; Table 3 shows MTI not always faster

Limited and circular analysis: Figure 4 is circular—applying CFG only to high-entropy tokens trivially shows modifications occur there; no ablation comparing selective at ω=1.5 vs. uniform at lower ω; missing comparison with temperature scaling on high-entropy tokens only

Questionable SOTA comparisons: Table 5 compares against methods with different design objectives (TALE: budget-aware, DEER: early stopping) without explaining why direct comparison is fair; limited baseline descriptions
Modest empirical gains: Improvements range 3-9% and are inconsistent (Table 2 shows high variance); no significance tests; unclear practical impact given hyperparameter tuning requirement

KV cache reuse unjustified: Appending 'OUTPUT ERROR' to cached conditional context does not create a valid unconditional distribution (unconditional should be independent of problem context); theoretical justification missing
Insufficient failure analysis: Only one case study (Fig. 6); no systematic characterization of when MTI fails; no breakdown by reasoning type or problem difficulty

Limited generalization evidence: High-entropy phenomenon demonstrated only on AIME2024; no verification across other benchmarks; threshold τ transfer across domains untested; vision-language eval limited to 3 spatial datasets

strengths: Clear and well-motivated empirical observation (Figure 1) showing errors concentrate in high-entropy tokens, providing solid foundation for the method
Elegant and practical solution combining selective CFG with lightweight KV cache reuse via negative prompts, eliminating overhead of dual-cache approaches

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple model families (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, Ling-mini), diverse task categories (general, coding, STEM), and 7+ benchmarks with consistent improvements (9.28% average on six tasks, 11.25% on AIME2024)

Strong ablation studies systematically analyzing entropy threshold τ, CFG strength ω, and negative prompt choices; Figure 4 provides principled justification that CFG is inherently ineffective on low-entropy tokens
Insightful analysis including word cloud visualization showing improved semantic diversity, case studies illustrating failure modes, and latency analysis demonstrating no actual slowdown
Excellent reproducibility with clear implementation details, comprehensive appendix, hyperparameter specifications, and promised code release
Plug-and-play design orthogonal to existing reasoning techniques, enabling composition with other test-time scaling methods
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: CFG for LLMs (Sanchez et al., 2023), entropy-based token selection (Wang et al., 2025; Lee et al., 2025a), and negative prompts (Koulischer et al., 2024) are all established; main contribution is their combination, which feels incremental

Incomplete theoretical justification for why high-entropy tokens drive errors and why 'OUTPUT ERROR' negatives specifically approximate a good unconditional branch; lacks mechanistic analysis of error propagation and formal justification for entropy as diagnostic metric

Hyperparameter tuning requirement: entropy threshold τ requires cross-validation per task/model pair, partially undermining 'training-free' claims; task-specific prompts (Table 8) improve results, suggesting domain knowledge helps despite generality claims

Insufficient statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; most benchmarks appear to be single runs; improvements of 1-3% may not be statistically robust, making it difficult to assess true effect sizes

Mixed SOTA comparisons (Table 5): results are competitive but not uniformly dominant; margins vary substantially across benchmarks (e.g., 78.3% vs. CGRS 61.1% on AIME2024-Qwen3-8B but only 95.8% vs. TALE 92.3% on MATH500)

Incomplete failure analysis: while Tables 1-2 show performance degradation at certain τ values, root causes are not investigated; case study only shows success; unclear when/why MTI fails or which reasoning types benefit most

Limited KV cache reuse analysis: paper claims reusing conditional cache with 'OUTPUT ERROR' better approximates unconditional branch than empty prompts but provides no quantitative analysis of approximation quality or comparison with proper unconditional computation
VLM extension feels preliminary: Table 4 shows only small gains (+1.8-3.0%) tested only on spatial reasoning, leaving unclear whether improvements generalize to broader multimodal reasoning tasks

Presentation could be tighter: some repetition between Sections 3.2-3.3, notation inconsistencies (c̄ vs c in Equation 1), dense Figure 2 that could be split, and slightly overstated claims (e.g., 'training-free' when τ requires tuning)
